_what: Trainer-shape throughput microbenchmark on the RTX 3080, run 2026-09-04 during the M10 plan review to test the plan's imported planning rate (560 examples/s, LEAF's realized A100 rate). RANDOM TOKEN IDS ONLY: no corpus text, no protected path, no teacher, no data loading, no evaluation. It bounds the hardware, not the pipeline; the day-one rate benchmark (mandate Compute) replaces it.
model: BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 + Linear(1152->1024) applied per token over mean-pooled concat of hidden layers 12/8/4, then masked mean pool + L2 normalize

bs32_mix7525_two_chunks_adamw.note: M9's collate: query and document chunks stepped separately

bs32_mix7525_two_chunks_fused_adamw.note: fused AdamW makes no difference; the cost is not the optimizer

bs32_single_padded_chunk_128.note: one padded chunk: 1.9x the two-chunk rate

bs128_mix7525_fused.note: 1.8x cheaper per example than bs32 single-chunk; family E must price this

bs512_mix7525_fused.note: past the launch-bound regime; no longer free

reading: At batch 32 with ~35-token queries the step is launch-bound, not FLOP-bound. The box meets or beats the rate the plan assumed for a rented A100, so the 2026-09-01 withdrawal of the box rested on M9's realized 226 examples/s, which was a pipeline artifact rather than a hardware limit. Two registered consequences: length-bucketed single-chunk batching is part of the build, and family E's verdict must be read against the 1.8x cost difference.
